text: Depending on the weapon or shield wielded, a specific type of damage is done.

Note that Attack Power and damage dealt is not the same thing, with the latter depending how the former compares with Defense. More specifically, if Attack Power is more than eight times as large as Defense then damage dealt is equal to 90% of Attack Power while if Attack Power is less than an eighth of Defense damage dealt is equal to 10% of Attack Power. In between these breakpoints the damage scaling is more granular: if Attack Power is greater than an eighth of Defense but less than the total Defense then damage dealt is equal to a point between 10% and 40% of Attack Power, if Attack Power is greater than the total Defense but less than two-and-a-half times the Defense then damage dealt is equal to a point between 40% and 70% of Attack Power, and if Attack Power is greater than two-and-a-half times the Defense but less than eight times the Defense then damage dealt is equal to a point between 70% and 90% of Attack Power.

text: Damage Negation (obtained through armor or items) and Defense (obtained through stats) both reduce the damage of incoming attacks. Each Damage Type has a corresponding defense stat and damage negation stat that governs its mitigation.

First, an incoming attack's Attack Power is compared with the target's Defense and a certain percentage of the Attack Power is left through as damage depending on the ratio (see the Attack Power section for further details). Afterwards, that damage is multiplied by the difference of one and the target's Damage Negation to determine the final damage dealt.

topics.title: Vigor
summary: Vigor (生命力, Seimeiryoku) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Vigor stat directly affects their HP totals. In addition, leveling Vigor will also increase Fire Defense, lessening the damage from Fire attacks, and also increases Immunity, increasing the Tarnished's resistance to Poison and Scarlet Rot.

The Tarnished can level Vigor by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Vigor has two soft cap points, 40 and 60, with HP, Fire Defense and Immunity gains experiencing sharp diminishing returns after both points.

topics.title: Mind
summary: Mind (精神力, Seishinryoku) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.
The Tarnished's Mind stat directly affects their FP totals. In addition, leveling Mind will also increase Focus, increasing the Tarnished's resistance to Sleep and Madness.

The Tarnished can level Mind by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Mind has a soft cap of 50 and 60 for increasing FP, and a soft cap of 40 and 60 for increasing Focus, with each derivative stat seeing diminishing returns after reaching these soft caps. Leveling Mind will not begin to see Focus returns until 31 and onwards.
A +0 Flask of Cerulean Tears replenishes 80 FP upon use, equivalent to 9/10 Mind, while a +12 Flask replenishes 220 FP, equivalent to 37/38 Mind.

Navy Hood grants +1 Mind.

topics.title: Endurance
summary: Endurance (持久力, Jikyūryoku) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Endurance stat directly affects their Stamina totals. Leveling Endurance will also increase the Tarnished's Robustness, which increases their resistance to Hemorrhage and Frostbite. Finally, Endurance also affects the Tarnished's possible Equip Load, increasing it as Endurance increases.

The Tarnished can level Endurance by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Endurance has three soft cap points for increasing Stamina, at 15, 30 and 50, with increases seeing dimishing returns after these points. Increasing Robustness sees two soft caps, 40 and 60, with gains from increasing Endurance not beginning until 31 Endurance onward. Increasing Equip Load sees soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance.

topics.title: Strength
summary: Strength (筋力 Kinryoku) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Strength stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Strength scaling. In addition, leveling Strength will also increase the Tarnished's Physical Defense.

The Tarnished can level Strength by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Strength has soft caps for raising Physical Defense at 30, 40 and 60 points. Soft caps for Strength scaling weapons varies by weapon type and affinities.

When two-handing a weapon Strength is increased by 50%, rounded up, for the purpose of scaling and meeting weapon requirements. A partial exception to this is paired weapons, such as all Fists and Claws, and the Ornamental Straight Sword, who will not get the boost to scaling. The Starscourge Greatsword, however, still receives the Strength bonus in spite of being a paired weapon. Skills do not get the Strength bonus for two-handing, with the exception of War Cry, Barbaric Roar, Shield Strike, Storm Assault, Shriek of Milos, Moonlight Greatsword (melee attack part only), Ice Lightning Sword, and Spinning Chain

Note that this Strength-boost also can be applied to Incantations via the Clawmark Seal, but that it doesn't apply to skills with a separate "bullet" attack that scales with Strength, such as Flame of the Redmanes, Ground Slam, or Storm Blade.

topics.title: Dexterity
summary: Dexterity (技量, Giryō) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Dexterity stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Dexterity scaling. Increasing Dexterity will also decrease the Tarnished's casting time with spells as it raises, with 70 Dexterity being the hardcap in order to achieve maximum casting speed on any spell. text: Virtual Dexterity is a hidden modifier in Elden Ring and a returning mechanic from Dark Souls III. Virtual Dexterity is a modifier added to certain weapons and items that raises the player's Dexterity stat, but only for the purpose of increasing their casting speed. Virtual Dexterity does not affect any other Dexterity-related mechanic such as weapon requirements, fall damage reduction, or Attack Power bonuses from scalings.

summary: Arcane (神秘, Shinpi) is one of the main attributes in Elden Ring.

It will also contribute to the Tarnished's Holy Defense and Vitality, which increases resistance to Death Blight.

topics.title: Equip Load
summary: Equip Load is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Equip Load affects their movement speed, and increases as the Tarnished equips more items in their equipment slots. It will also affect the amount of invincibility frames and recovery frames, with heavier equipped loads affecting them negatively. More specifically, Light Load rolls and Medium Load rolls are equally effective and have the same recovery time, but the former will roll a longer distance. Heavy Load rolls meanwhile face an almost twice as long recovery animation, leaving the Tarnished very vulnerable to follow-up attacks.

Equipped items totalling less than 30% of the maximum equip load is considered a Light Load. Greater than 30% and less than 70% is considered a Medium Load. Greater than 70% is considered a Heavy Load. The game menu will display the Tarnished's current load type directly under the numerical weight totals.
Exceeding 100% weight load will result in being Overloaded, rendering the Tarnished unable to roll or backstep, instead only staggering forward slightly with no benefit.
Equip Load exceeding 70% also increases the time it takes to recover Stamina as well and increases harm caused by fall damage.

The Tarnished can increase their maximum Equip Load by leveling Endurance. Equip Load experiences soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance, resulting in diminishing returns as leveling increases past these points.
A Prophet has the lowest starting equip load due to its starting Endurance of 8, while the Samurai has the highest due to its Endurance being at 13.
While all other classes start in Medium Load thanks to their starting equipment, the Vagabond is the only class to start in Heavy Load due to its heavy equipment.

The scaling is strongest early on, around 1.5-1.6 per point of Endurance below 26 points in the Attribute before falling off from 26 to 38 Endurance before recovering and averaging 1.5 from 39 to 60 Endurance before falling down 1.0 Equip Load per point of Endurance above 61.

topics.title: Discovery
summary: Discovery is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Discovery affects their ability to find drops from defeated enemies. Discovery has a base level of 100 for the Tarnished, and Discovery can be raised by 1 for each point of Arcane taken while leveling up. Equipment can also boost Discovery while worn. Additionally, Discovery can be boosted temporarily by using a Silver-Pickled Fowl Foot consumbale item.
An item with a P% drop rate is actually found with probability as follows, if you have Discovery D:
\begin{align}
Chance &= \frac{100\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}{1000+ \left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor-10P} \\
&= \frac{100}{1+\frac{1000-10P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
&= \frac{10}{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{100-P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
\end{align}

summary: Memory Slots is a base stat in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished has two Memory Slots by default, and this amount can be increased through finding Memory Stones throughout the Lands Between. There is also a Talisman, Moon of Nokstella, which will increase the Tarnished's Memory Slots by 2. topics.title: Poise
summary: Poise is one of the stats and hidden mechanic for enemies in Elden Ring. It determines when a player character will stagger or when an enemy character will be stance broken. It is often confused with Damage Level, a separate mechanic that determines if an enemy will be staggered after a single attack.

text: Tarnished Poise is a player statistic that is granted by equipping heavier armor, using the Bull-Goat's Talisman, and other effects. It is the statistic that determines whether a player is staggered when hit by an attack, when taking an attack the players poise is reduced by the attack's poise damage, and at zero poise the player staggers and poise resets. Poise will begin regenerating after not being hit by an attack for 30 seconds, as a result in active combat Poise regeneration is rarely a factor and Poise will normally only be reset after a stagger.

For PvE purposes, practically all enemy attacks in Elden Ring deal either 50 poise damage, 100 poise damage or much higher, meaning that the breakpoints of 51 poise (which can take one normal attack without hitting zero) and 101 poise (which can take two attacks or one strong attack without hitting zero) are almost all that matters, the difference between 51 and 90 poise is essentially nil as both will stagger after 2 normal attacks.

Certain actions have Hyper Armor, which adds an extra amount of Poise for a certain part of those actions (usually depending on the weapon used). A select few actions have Super Armor, most notably the Skill: Lion's Claw, letting their user effectively ignore Poise.

All enemies in Elden Ring have a hidden Poise meter, which ranges from 15 to 65 for normal enemies and 80 to 120 for bosses with some notable exceptions. Attacks on the enemy deal damage to their poise independent from the actual damage (with the notable exception of the Furnace Golem), with generally heavier attacks dealing more poise damage. An enemy's Poise will start regenerating at 13 poise per second after an amount of time equal to their base Poise divided by 13, so a normal enemy with 65 poise will start regenerating after 5 seconds and a boss with 120 Poise will start regenerating after 9.2 seconds.

If an enemy's Poise reaches zero then they will be stance broken and will be stunned for a significant amount of time, most enemies will also now have a weak spot where a player can do a riposte by performing a light attack, which will perform a critical hit for a significant chunk of damage and knock the enemy back, resetting their Poise and taking them out of the stun. Generally the highest damage combo from a stance break will be to execute as many attacks as possible whilst the enemy is stunned, and then riposte for the final hit, however if unfamiliar with a boss and their exact stun duration just doing a riposte is advisable as that is the biggest chunk of damage.

Notable Poise outliers include Starscourge Radahn with 200 Poise, which being the highest base poise also has the longest regeneration delay of 15.4 seconds, Lichdragon Fortissax with 350 effective Poise (140 base Poise health but only takes 40% Poise damage most attacks and 80% Poise damage on headshots), Night's Cavalry with 400 effective Poise (80 base Poise but only takes 20% Poise damage from all attacks), and Ancient Dragons (including named ones) with 600 effective Poise (120 base Poise but only takes 20% Poise damage from most attacks and 80% Poise damage on headshots). Furnace Golems do not stance break based on Poise damage but instead based on total regular damage done to them.

topics.title: Blood Loss
summary: Blood Loss (出血, Shukketsu), also known as Hemorrhage, is a status ailment in Elden Ring and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN that inflicts a burst of damage.

text: Blood Loss is usually caused by serrated, thorned, exremely sharp, or bloodstained weapons. Spells and items affiliated with the Lord of Blood also cause this status effect.

Deals a combination of flat and percentage damage when inflicted. Humanoid enemies, smaller enemies, and Tarnished are also staggered. The flat damage is usually 100, but it increases to 200 when done by a Somber Smithing Stone-upgraded weapon with innate Blood Loss and Arcane-scaling or by a regular Smithing Stone-upgraded with innate Blood Loss and the Blood-affinity. The percentage damage depends on the enemy: normal enemies and Tarnished take 15% damage, bosses and enemies that directly accompany them take 10.5% damage, and the Lord of Blood takes 7.5% damage.

Additionally, the blood loss inflicted by Mohg's Nihil attack is unique and only inflicts percentage damage, roughly 33% damage on each of the first two pulses and about 66% on the final pulse. Using the Purifying Crystal Tear greatly reduces this damage to about 5% on the first two pulses and 10% on the final one.
Blood loss can also be inflicted on someone in the middle of invincibility frames, such as a roll, though this only causes the stun and not the damage.
Resistance to this status ailment is governed by Robustness.

topics.title: Poison
summary: Poison (毒, Doku) is a status ailment in Elden Ring and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN that inflicts damage over time, similar to Scarlet Rot.

text: Poison accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Poison to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off. The damage dealt more of than not depends on the type of poison used, but it can differ depending on the type of weapon or tool used, and the enemy inflicting the poison.
The most common damage formula for normal Poison is (0.07% Max HP) + 7 per second over the course of 90 seconds, which totals to (6.3% Max HP) + 630 damage over the course of its full duration.
Some enemies inflict a stronger type of normal Poison that deals (0.42% Max HP) + 18 per second for 30 seconds, totaling (12.6% Max HP) + 540 damage over its full duration.

Deadly Poison caused by the Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle Shadow of the Erdtree, the Serpentbone Blade, the Tooth Whip and the Venomous Fang deals (0.14% Max HP) + 14 per second for 30 seconds, for a total of (4.2% Max HP) + 420 damage over the course of its full duration.

Deadly Poison caused by the Fetid Pot, Hefty Fetid Pot Shadow of the Erdtree and the Roped Fetid Pot, Deadly Poison inflicts (0.14% Max HP) + 12 per second for 30 seconds, totaling (4.2% Max HP) + 360 damage over its full duration.
The tool Poison Spraymist inflicts Deadly Poison that deals (0.21% Max HP) + 21 for 30 seconds, for a total of (6.3% Max HP) + 630 damage over its full duration, making it stronger than Scarlet Rot.
The damage received from poison can vary greatly depending on the source and the target inflicted. In general, poison is split up into two categories: Normal and Deadly.
Normal poison is generally the most common and is automatically granted to any weapon that has it's affinity changed to Poison with one exception.

Deadly poison is innate to the weapons that already come with it and damages it's targets at a faster rate than normal poison. However, it does not last as long and the total damage received from a single proc of Deadly Poison is ultimately lower than Normal Poison.
Resistance to this status ailment is governed by Immunity.

topics.title: Scarlet Rot
summary: Scarlet Rot (朱い腐敗, Akai Fuhai) is a status ailment in Elden Ring and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN that inflicts a significant amount of damage over time, similar to Poison.

text: Scarlet Rot is an old legend in the Lands Between, a dangerous sickness that eats away life like a vicious plague. It corrupts men and beasts who come into contact with it, deforming their bodies and eating away their wits, driving them to madness and causing them to act like wild animals. Those afflicted with the Scarlet Rot such as Millicent also suffer from nightmares due to the affliction. Areas afflicted with Scarlet Rot sprout fungal growths or flower buds. As such, Scarlet Rot is often fended off using fire.

The Empyrean and demigod, Malenia, Blade of Miquella harbored the affliction of Scarlet Rot within her body from birth, which has decayed her body and caused her to lose her limbs. Her will, pride, dignity, and sense of self, along with the help of her brother Miquella of the Haligtree's Unalloyed Gold Needle assisted with resisting the call of the Scarlet Rot. However, at the Battle of Aeonia, the final battle of the Shattering, she abandoned this pride to meet Starscourge Radahn's measure. This resulted in the blooming of the first flower of Aeonia causing both Caelid and Radahn to become blighted by the Scarlet Rot. Upon Malenia's return to Miquella's Haligtree, it too was infected and malformed by the Scarlet Rot. The Swamp of Aeonia spawned by the flower in Caelid gave rise to Kindred of Rot, also known as "Pests." Some inorganic beings are capable of contracting and hosting the disease; a number of Crystalians, and their weapons, fester with Scarlet Rot.

Despite the horrific effects of the sickness, some worship the Scarlet Rot as a god. The sickly Maleigh Marais of the Shaded Castle was a private believer, and considered Malenia his personal goddess. To those enraptured by the Scarlet Rot, the mushrooms that spawn from it growing on their bodies are holy vestments that root them to the earth. Long ago, great lords served the Scarlet Rot, perhaps with such large fungal bodies serving as their crowns. Ever since the Battle of Aeonia, Sage Gowry has dedicated himself to the resplendence of the Order of Rot, the cycle of decay and rebirth, desiring Malenia to bloom into a goddess, and her daughters to join her as scarlet valkyries.

Long ago, Malenia's mentor, the Blind Swordsman, sealed away an ancient god that was Rot itself using a flowing sword bestowed upon him by a fairy in legend. The divine essence of this Outer God was sealed in the Lake of Rot in the Ainsel River deep below Liurnia of the Lakes.
The head confessor Crepus, an assassin of the Roundtable Hold serving the Two Fingers, used bolts imbued with Scarlet Rot with his Black-Key Crossbow.

Scarlet Rot accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Scarlet Rot to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off.
Resistance to this status ailment is governed by Immunity.

topics.title: Sleep
summary: Sleep (睡眠, Suimin) is a status ailment in Elden Ring and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN that temporarily incapacitates enemies weak to sleep. Enemies with stronger resistance and Tarnished are stunned instead. Tarnished also receive damage to their focus points.

text: Inflicting Sleep on a player will briefly stagger them, even through a roll, and drains FP equal to 30 + 10% of max FP.
Inflicting on most generic enemies will briefly stagger them.
If the player is inflicted with Sleep while riding Torrent, they will be instantly knocked off.

Sleep has special interactions with certain enemies: some, like the Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble, Vulgar Militia, and Mad Pumpkin Heads, will fall into a heavier sleep, making them vulnerable to a Critical Attack and potentially sleeping for up to a minute if not damaged. Others, enemies that ride other entities, will get knocked off their mount. This includes almost all enemies on horseback (such as Godrick Knights, Cuckoo Knights, Leyndell Knights, and Kaiden Sellswords) but also the Giant Ant-riding Nox Swordstresses but doesn't include Night's Cavalry (since they are immune to Sleep) or Tree Sentinels (since them and their horse are effectively one entity).
[Eternal Sleep]

A special variant of Sleep introduced with Shadow of the Erdtree, Eternal Sleep has slightly different effects from regular Sleep. The FP drain to players is increased to 50 + 15% of max FP, weaker enemies such as Godrick Soldiers can potentially be slept permanently and never wake up, and bosses vulnerable to Sleep won't wake up the until 5 seconds after they were first attacked and aren't susceptible to Critical Attacks.
Resistance to this status ailment is governed by Focus.

topics.title: Immunity
summary: Immunity (免疫, Men'eki) is a resistance stat in Elden Ring.
Immunity governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Poison and Scarlet Rot. It will not decrease the amount of damage taken once afflicted by Poison or Scarlet Rot.

The Tarnished's base Immunity is two parts, with each part determined by their Level and Vigor attribute. The sum of the two parts is what is displayed on the Status screen. The Tarnished's Immunity will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161, which will see dimishing returns based on level as the level increases. Vigor does not begin to directly affect Immunity until Level 31, at which point the resulting increase from Vigor will be added to the total base Immunity displayed.
From 31-40 Vigor: +3 Immunity each level
From 41-60 Vigor: +0.5 Immunity each level
From 61-99 Vigor: +0.25 Immunity each level
Immunity is further increases by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.
Immunity can be temporarily be increased by consuming Immunizing Cured Meat, Immunizing White Cured Meat and Dappled Cured Meat.

topics.title: Robustness
summary: Robustness is a resistance stat in Elden Ring.

Robustness governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Blood Loss and Frostbite status ailments. It will not decrease the amount of damage taken once afflicted by Blood Loss or Frostbite.

The Tarnished's base Robustness is the sum total of two different parts, with each part determined by their Level and Endurance attribute. The first part is calculated based on the Tarnished's level. Their Robustness will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161. The second part is calculated based off of the Tarnished's Endurance stat, which will begin directly increasing the Tarnished's Robustness from 31 Endurance and up. The total of these two parts is what is displayed on the status screen.
Raising Endurance to increase Robustness has soft caps at 40 and 60 Endurance.
From 31-40 Endurance: +3 Robustness each level
From 41-60 Endurance: +0.5 Robustness each level
From 61-99 Endurance: +0.25 Robustness each level
Robustness is further increased by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.
Robustness can be temporarily increased by consuming Invigorating Cured Meat, Invigorating White Cured Meat and Dappled Cured Meat.

topics.title: Damage Type
summary: There are several Damage Types in Elden Ring, divided by being either Physical or Elemental.

text: Standard is the damage dealt by attacks that are neither particularly sharp, nor heavy, nor thin, such as those from Axes and Straight Swords.
Strike is the damage dealt by heavy and blunt attacks, such as those from Hammers and many Colossal Weapons.
Slash is the damage dealt by sharp attacks, such as those from Claws and Curved Swords.
Pierce is the damage dealt by thrusting attacks, such as those from Thrusting Swords and Spears. They have the additional benefit of dealing increased damage against attacking foes.
Fire is the damage dealt by flaming attacks, and are common among Incantations and Torches.
Holy is the damage dealt by bright golden attacks, and are common among Incantations and Weapons associated with the Erdtree, the various Two Fingers, and the Rune of Death.
Lightning is the damage dealt by attacks that sparkle with yellow or red lightning, and are common among Incantations and weapons associated with Ancient Dragons.
Magic is the damage dealt by Frostbite-based and blue or turqoise attacks, and are most common among Sorceries.

text: Glintstone Sorceries are the most straightforward method to fight with magic damage. Nearly all sorceries, with very few exceptions (Gelmir Sorceries and most Gravity Sorceries), deal magic damage.
There are also many Somberstone weapons with an Intelligence scaling and scaling in Strength and Dexterity.
The Watchdog's Staff is a Somberstone weapon that scales the best with Strength. Its unique skill only scales with weapon level, not Intelligence, making it a viable option for Strength builds.

Craftable items are also an option, but since most magical throwing items scale off of Intelligence, it would be the more intelligent move to stick with sorceries if one already has the specs for it. However, Crystal Darts can turn imps and even Erdtree Burial Watchdogs (in the duo fight only) into temporary allies. Intelligence is unnecessary for the effect to work.
Glintstone Breath and Smarag's Glintstone Breath are powerful options for Faith builds to deal magic damage, though they require slight investment in Arcane.
[Who is Weak to Magic?]
Wildlife are typically 40% weaker to Magic Damage.
Hostile beasts will typically have a 20% weakness to it, like Dogs and Land Octopi.
[Who is Strong Against Magic?]
As a general rule of thumb, enemies that deal a certain damage type are resistant to said damage type.
For Magic, this may include Glintstone Sorcerers. Loretta and Rellana, Twin Moon Knight are two examples of bosses that cast Glintstone Sorceries and are resistant Magic damage.
The two dragons in Elden Ring that can breathe Glintstone Breath are Smarag and Adula. They both infamously boast an 80% resistance to Magic damage.
Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear, increases Magic damage dealt by 20% (12.5% in PvP) for 3 minutes when used with the Flask of Wondrous Physick.

topics.title: Weapon Scaling
summary: Scaling is a mechanic in Elden Ring. Most weapons possess scaling values, which cause the weapon's effectiveness to increase in accordance with an associated stat. Weapons can scale with Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith or Arcane. Scaling affinity with each stat is signified by a letter icon on the weapon's information.
Attribute scaling impacts:
Attack Power
Sorcery Scaling and Incantation Scaling, with the base damage calculated as 100 since the actual damage varies by spell
Poison, Blood Loss, Sleep, and Madness, if the weapon has Arcane attribute scaling
Scaling doesn't affect poise damage or stamina damage.

text: The letter grades that are used to represent a weapon's scaling affinity is only a rough guide of a weapon's potential. These grades are derived from a scaling value, which is an invisible number that determines the exact amount of damage you receive from scaling. The scaling values that each letter can represent are:
The formula for calculating a weapon's scaling damage is:
Scaling value*Base damage\left (\frac{stat scaling}{100} \right)

Base damage is the damage of the weapon before any scaling is applied, and stat scaling is a value that is gained by increasing the relevant attribute. Increasing both of these values will also increase the bonus damage received from scaling, which means that a weapon with lower base damage but a higher scaling value will not necessarily gain more scaling.
[Attribute Requirements]

Most weapons have a minimum requirement for each attribute they scale with. If that requirement is not met, anything that scales with that attribute receives no scaling, and instead takes a -40% penalty.
For example, the Club has 103 base Physical Attack Power, and Strength scaling with a requirement of 10. A character with only 9 Strength would have 61 Physical Attack Power (103 - 42).
[Stat Scaling]

This value increases as the associated stat increases, varying somewhat depending on if the used affinity is physical (Standard, Heavy, Keen, Quality, or Occult) or non-physical (Fire, Flame Art, Lightning, Sacred, Magic, Cold, Blood, or Poison).
;Physical affinity values
Stat at 10: 15
Stat at 20: 35
Stat at 30: 46.5
Stat at 40: 57.5
Stat at 50: 67.5
Stat at 60: 75
Stat at 70: 82.5
Stat at 80: 90
Stat at 90: 92.5
Stat at 99: 96

As can be seen, for physical affinities the biggest increase is from increasing a stat from 10 to 20, before falling of bit-by-bit from 20 to 40, then 40 to 50, and then 50 to 80, until it finally slows down to a crawl from 80 to 99.
;Non-physical affinity values
Stat at 10: 19
Stat at 20: 40
Stat at 30: 53
Stat at 40: 66.5
Stat at 50: 80
Stat at 60: 85
Stat at 70: 90
Stat at 80: 95
Stat at 90: 97.5
Stat at 99: 100

For non-physical affinities, however, the increase is more steady. It still falls of heavily after the 10 to 20 stretch but after that remains steady with the scaling (most notably reaching the same amount of scaling by 50 as physical affinities don't get until almost reaching 70) until reaching 50, where after the scaling slows down to less than half until the stat reaches 80 and halves against for the final stretch to reach 99.
;Spell tools

Spell tools (Staves and Sacred Seals) uses one of three different scaling rates depending on whether or not they scale with only one stat, scales with more than one stat, or if it's the Demi-Human Queen's Staff. The exception to this is the Prince of Death's Staff (PDS) which despite being a Staff that scales with more than one stat uses the more backloaded "one stat" scaling, making it require a large amount of both Intelligence and Faith to attain good results.

More specifically, those that scales with one stat (and the PDS) start strong and gain stronger scaling after reaching 25 in the stat and then again after reaching 60, until finally dropping off hard upon eventually reaching 80 in that stat.

Scaling with more than one stat initially scales rather poorly before skyrocketing to being much, much stronger in scaling for a stat upon getting to 15 in that stat until 30, were after it falls to more normal, "one stat" levels of scaling and then increases become insignificant after reaching 45 in that stat.

The Demi-Human Queen's Staff is effectively the inverse of regular "one stat" scaling with exceptional scaling prior to reaching 20 in Intelligence and then being weaker until it reaches 40 and after that it becomes even weaker.
;Status Effects scaling

All weapons increase their scaling values by being upgraded. All weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones gain an extra 8% of their base scaling per upgrade level, while other weapons gain 2% by default.

Weapons that can be infused with ashes of war can gain affinities which alter both the base damage and the scaling values, affecting how different stats increase scaling damage. There is no universal formula for how infusion changes the values of a weapon and different weapons are changed by an infusion in different, seemingly arbitrary ways.

topics.title: Affinities
summary: Affinities are a mechanic in Elden Ring that alters a weapon's properties after applying Ashes of War.

text: All Affinities except for Standard, Heavy, Keen, and Quality (the "basic four") will prevent Weapon Buffs from being applied to a weapon (except for those applied via a skill), and will also limit the amount of compatible skills.
More specifically:
→ Magic and Cold skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Magic or Cold affinity.
→ Fire and Flame Art skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Fire or Flame Art affinity.
→ Lightning and Sacred skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Lightning or Sacred affinity.
→ Poison, Blood, and Occult skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Poison, Blood, or Occult affinity.

topics.title: Affinity/Standard
summary: Standard is an affinity in Elden Ring.

This is the default affinity of all infusable weapons except for the Butchering Knife, which is Sacred by default. It provides a weapon's default scaling modifiers, a mix of Strength-scaling and Dexterity-scaling.

The Standard Affinity is compatible with all Skills by default, even without any of the Whetblades. It is the affinity of all Ashes of War exclusive to ranged weapons (Light Bows, Bows, and Greatbows), and to Perfume Bottles Shadow of the Erdtree and Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree weapons.

It's also the affinity of the vast majority of shield and parry Ash of Wars (mostly exclusive to Small Shields, Medium Shields, Greatshields, and Thrusting Shields, though the latter two cannot accept parry-based ashes) except for Ash of War: Carian Retaliation and Ash of War: Thops's Barrier (both Magic affinity), and Ash of War: Golden Parry, Ash of War: Holy Ground, and Ash of War: Vow of the Indomitable (all three Sacred affinity).

text: A few weapons are upgraded with regular Smithing Stones but cannot have their affinity changed from Standard or be infused with an Ash of War.

These include the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle Daggers, the Forked-Tongue Hatchet Shadow of the Erdtree and Ripple Blade Axes, the Troll's Hammer Colossal Weapon, the Treespear Great Spear, and the Ripple Crescent Halberd Halberd.
Perfume Bottles and all Ranged Weapons that upgraded with regular Smithing Stones are also locked to Standard Affinity, however they can all accept a decently wide variety of Ashes of War.

For any skill with damage separate from the weapon itself, such as Skill: Beast's Roar and Skill: Flame of the Redmanes, it provides neutral scaling for Intelligence-, Faith-, and Arcane-scaling skills but slightly decreased scaling for Strength- and Dexterity-scaling skills.

topics.title: Affinity/Heavy
summary: Heavy is an affinity in Elden Ring.
It is a Physical-focused affinity that slightly decreases base damage, removes Dexterity-scaling, and decreases all other scalings, in exchange for greatly increasing Strength-scaling.
It's compatible with all skills, provided that the Iron Whetblade has been acquired.
Its associated Ash of War skills are generally either only available to larger weapons or universally available.

text: The Heavy Affinity Bullet skills (the entirety Kick, the landing and shockwave of Ground Slam, the shockwave of Earthshaker, both slams of Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker, and the initial roar of Troll's Roar) scale entirely with the wielder's Strength (and the weapon's upgrade level), strengthened by the weapon's Affinity. Heavy Affinity itself unsurprisingly has the strongest scaling for these skills, while Fire Affinity is a bit weaker, and Quality, Cold, Poison, and Blood Affinity are slightly weaker than that. Meanwhile, Keen, Lightning, and Magic Affinity weaken the Strength-scaling of these skills. Heavy Affinity also entirely removes a Bullet skill's Dexterity-scaling, which affects Keen and Lightning Affinity Bullet skills and partially affects Quality and Cold Affinity Bullet skills.

Additionally, Heavy Affinity is good for the skills of other, Strength-scaling Affinities: for Fire Affinity in particular Heavy Affinity is actually the strongest option for the bullet skills (the initial flame wave of Flaming Strike, the entirety Flame of the Redmanes, the flaming pool from Eruption, and throughout Prelate's Charge), while for Quality Affinity it's bullet skills (the wind blade from Storm Blade, the vacuum wave from Vacuum Slice, and the phantom from Phantom Slash) do second best with Heavy Affinity, being outmatched by Keen Affinity but outmatching Quality Affinity itself until very high levels of both Strength and Dexterity.
["Weak" Heavy weapons]

Certain weapons that have their weapon Attack Power lean towards are considered "weak" with the Heavy Affinity. This means that they have weaker Strength-scaling for bullet skills while the weapon is using Heavy Affinity, resulting in a penalty to Attack Power for these skills of roughly 2-3%. However, unlike the weapons considered "weak" with the Keen Affinity this actually has a small advantage, as they in return gain a slight Dexterity-scaling for Keen, Quality, Lightning, and Cold Affinity skills, resulting in a small Attack Power bonus compared to regular Heavy Affinity weapons (though Quality Affinity Bullet skills are mostly just brought up to par, unless Dexterity is a good bit above 10).
Note that this only applies to these weapons when using the Heavy Affinity, any other Affinities are not affected.

topics.title: Affinity/Keen
summary: Keen is an affinity in Elden Ring.
It is a Physical-focused affinity that slightly decreases base damage, and heavily decreases Strength-scaling and decreases all other scalings, in exchange for greatly increasing Dexterity-scaling.
It's compatible with all skills, provided that the Iron Whetblade has been acquired.

Its associated Ash of War skills are generally either only available to large-sized or smaller weapons or universally available, as well as skills exclusive to Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree.

text: The Keen Affinity Bullet skills (the projectile from Beast's Roar) scale entirely with the wielder's Dexterity (and the weapon's upgrade level), strengthened by the weapon's Affinity. Keen Affinity itself unsurprisingly has the strongest scaling for these skills, while Lightning Affinity is a bit weaker, and Quality, Cold, Poison, and Blood Affinity are slightly weaker than that. Meanwhile, Heavy, Fire, and Magic Affinity weaken the Dexterity-scaling of these skills. Keen Affinity also weakens a Bullet skill's Strength-scaling, which affects Heavy and Fire Affinity Bullet skills and partially affects Quality Affinity Bullet skills.

Additionally, Keen Affinity is good for the skills of other, Dexterity-scaling Affinities: for Lightning Affinity (the bolt from Thunderbolt, the lightning bolt part of Lightning Slash, the lightning dash from Blinkbolt, and the roll part of Lightning Ram), Cold Affinity (the projectile from Ice Spear, the orbs, trails, and explosions from Ghostflame Call, the spread and explosion of Hoarfrost Stomp, and the spread and explosion of Divine Beast Frost Stomp), and Quality Affinity (the wind blade from Storm Blade, the vacuum wave from Vacuum Slice, and the phantom from Phantom Slash) Keen Affinity is actually the strongest option for the bullet skills.
["Weak" Keen weapons]

Certain weapons that have their weapon Attack Power lean towards are considered "weak" with the Keen Affinity. This means that they have weaker Dexterity-scaling for bullet skills while the weapon is using Keen Affinity, resulting in a penalty to Attack Power for these skills of roughly 2-3%. Unlike the weapons considered "weak" with the Heavy Affinity, there is no upside to this.
Note that this only applies to these weapons when using the Keen Affinity, any other Affinities are not affected.

It's compatible with Heavy, Keen, Quality, Blood, and Occult skills, provided that the Black Whetblade has been acquired.
Its associated Ash of War skills are unsurprisingly focued on inflicting Poison, with some also being able to detonate the status effect for extra damage in exchange for removing it early.

The Warped Axe and Sword Lance have higher build-up than expected, on par with a Greataxe instead of an Axe and on par with a Colossal Sword instead of a Heavy Thrusting Sword respectively.

topics.title: Smithing Stones
summary: Smithing Stones are Bolstering Materials in Elden Ring, of which 9 variants exist.

They can be used by Smithing Master Hewg or War Counselor Iji to incrementally upgrade Weapons in exchange for runes, up to +25, consuming the stones in the process. Every "tier" of Smithing Stone can upgrade an armament up to 3 times before the next tier of Smithing Stone is needed; the first upgrade of a tier requires 2 stones, the second 4, and the third 6. Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones are the sole exception — only being used once to upgrade weapons from +24 to +25.
However, for certain special armaments, the rarer Somber Smithing Stones are needed instead; such armaments can only be upgraded to +10, and only require one somber stone per upgrade.

They can be found scattered through both the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, sometimes looted from certain enemies when killed, or purchased from some Merchants in usually limited quantity. However, excepting Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones, they can be purchased in unlimited quantity from the Twin Maiden Husks after giving them Smithing-Stone Miner's Bell Bearings, of which 4 are scattered throughout the Lands Between.

topics.title: Somber Smithing Stones
summary: Somber Smithing Stones (also simply known as Somberstones) are Bolstering Materials in Elden Ring, of which 10 variants exist. They are rarer counterparts of ordinary Smithing Stones required for upgrading certain special Weapons.

They can be used by Smithing Master Hewg or War Counselor Iji to incrementally upgrade such special Weapons in exchange for runes, up to +10, consuming one stone in the process. Each "tier" of Somber Smithing Stone can upgrade an armament once, to the same level as the number in their name. Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones are the sole exception to this naming scheme, being the equivalent of a Somber Smithing Stone 10.

However, for ordinary armaments, regular Smithing Stones are needed instead; such armaments can be upgraded all the way to +25, and require 12 stones per 3 upgrades, except for the final one which only requires 1 Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

They can be found scattered through both the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, sometimes looted from certain enemies when killed, or purchased from some Merchants in usually limited quantity. However, excepting Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones, they can be purchased in unlimited quantity from the Twin Maiden Husks after giving them Somberstone Miner's Bell Bearings, of which 4 are scattered throughout the Lands Between.

topics.title: Buffs
summary: Buffs are effects applied by a Tarnished to either themself or to themself and their allies, and are used to strengthen offense or defense.

They come in six categories: Weapon Buffs, Body Buffs, Aura Buffs, Health Regeneration Buffs, Variant Buffs, and Unique Buffs. Except for the last two categories, at most one Buff per category can be active at a time and activating another Buff of the same category will remove the older one.

text: All Weapon Buffs are self-targeted, and almost all of them have only offensive benefits, with very few exceptions. They cannot be applied to any type of ranged weapon or casting implement, and only a few specific ones can be used on shields (except for Thrusting Shields, which are eligible for both).

It's possible to keep two weapons buffed at the same time by two-handing the left-hand weapon and using either a Grease or a Skill on it, then stopping the two-handing so that the right-hand weapon also can be buffed with either a Grease or a Skill. It isn't necessary to use the same buff category for both weapons.

Some weapons are buffable and some aren't. As a general rule, weapons upgraded with Smithing Stones are buffable while weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones aren't buffable with anything except their innate skill if it grants them a weapon buff. Exceptions to this rule are the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle, two Smithing Stone weapons that aren't buffable, and the Bloodhound's Fang, Varré's Bouquet, and Bonny Butchering Knife, three Somber Smithing Stone weapons that are buffable.

Additionally, weapons equipped with affinities that aren't either Standard, Heavy, Keen, or Quality also aren't buffable except for with the Skills that are compatible with those affinities, with no exceptions.
For Weapon Buffs that are also either Sorceries or Incantations, they can only be cast on right-handed weapons (or left-handed shields for the shield-specific ones).
[Shield Buffs]

Shield Buffs are a small subtype of defensive Weapon Buffs that are only usable for Shields, though the difference is really only important for Thrusting Shields since they can use both Shield Buffs and regular Weapon Buffs and thus might accidentally overwrite one with the other.

text: The damage dealt by skills is subject to scaling depending on the nature of the skill and whether the user has sufficient FP. For skills that directly attack with the weapon, the weapon's actual attack power modified by the skill's Motion Value. Some skills, such as Eruption or Loretta's Slash will also provide an additional damage bonus to the attack that scales with the weapon's scaling values where appropriate (Strength for fire damage, Intelligence for magic, etc). Refer to the individual skills pages for more information.

Skills that deal damage in any way other than directly hitting with the weapon perform differently, instead using special bullet colliders specific to the skill. These skills generally perform the same regardless of the weapon and are only affected by the weapon's upgrade level, the weapon's affinity and one or two stats related to the skill's associated affinity. Quality skills scale with Strength and Dexterity, magic skills scale with Intelligence, and so on. The actual scaling values are independent of the weapon's own scaling, with the exception of certain weapons using Heavy or Keen affinities. Unique weapon skills behave differently, often scaling the bullets with the weapon's attack power.

Heavy affinity affords the strongest scaling value for Strength, the same holds true for Keen with Dexterity, Magic for Intelligence, and Occult for Arcane. Although the Fire and Lightning affinities provide improved scaling with their associated stats compared to Standard, they are outperformed in bullet damage by Heavy and Keen respectively. Poison and Blood affinities actually provide worse Arcane scaling than Standard but improved scaling with every other stat. For most weapons Heavy affinity has no Dexterity scaling at all.

A selection of weapons use alternate bullet affinity for Heavy and Keen affinities that scale slightly worse with the main stat. These are typically weapons already strongly aligned toward Strength or Dexterity. As a result Beast's Roar or Thunderbolt will deal more damage when used on a Keen Claymore than a Keen Dagger. Weapons with the alternate Heavy bullet scaling actually have better Dexterity bullet scaling than weapons with the normal Heavy affinity bullet scaling (it's the same Dexterity scaling as Fire affinity). These weapons will perform better with Quality, Keen and Cold scaling bullets while infused with a Heavy affinity than normal Heavy weapons, but still worse than weapons with the appropriate affinity.

topics.title: Paired Weapons
summary: Paired Weapons (also commonly referred to as "Dual Wielding" or "Power-Stancing") is a player-ability in which two armaments of the same armament type are being wielded in both hands at the same time, gaining access to new attacks which involve both weapons being swung at once from singular inputs.
Paired attacks are usually performed with the following inputs by default depending on the platform: on PlayStation. on XBOX. on PC with keyboard and mouse.
__TOC__

text: Video clips of the other paired weapon movesets will be added to this section as recordings have been gathered and processed.

Some armaments do not have the ability to be two-handed like most others. If the player tries to two-hand these weapons, then their character will instead pull out a a copy of the same weapon in the other hand. This aspect give these weapons some unique properties to them with some being beneficial and others detrimental:

Gives the player an easier and less resource-intensive means to access paired movesets, as they need only to occupy one single armament slot and has a weight equivalent to that of a single weapon, effectively reducing ones carried Equip Load.
→ Being singular weapons also spares the player from spending twice the amount of Smithing Stones to gain access to their paired movesets while also maintaining a viable damage output.
→ Weapon buffs such as grease being used on these kinds of paired armaments also applies the status bonus to both copies of the weapon at once.
The / / inputs now use the paired attack animations.

→ This means the weapons does not have immediate access to the one-handed attacks, as their one-handed inputs are currently occupied by paired attacks nor do they have access to the benefits of two-handed attacks, like the increased hyper-armor found on larger weapons or the beneficial effects received from the Two-Handed Sword Talisman.
The / / inputs will make the player character guard, with the exception of Rellana's Twin Blades, which will instead attack with the left-handed fire sword.

→ This is usually a detriment on most of the lighter weapons due to their low guarded damage negation and guard boost stats. The Deflecting Hardtear can significantly mitigate this issue however and make guard counterattacks a viable asset to one's tool set.

The strong attack animations incorporate swings with both weapons at once on the following armament types: Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree Fists Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree Claws Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree Perfume Bottles Shadow of the Erdtree

→ The Ornamental Straight Sword also gains a unique Strong Dash Attack when in it's "two-handed" paired stance. It can also gain a unique neutral strong attack and charged attack as well, however the Unique Skill: Golden Tempering ability needs to be active for those moves to become accessible.
→ Grafted Dragon is the only Fist type weapon that doesn't allow the player to pull out a duplicate of itself with only a single slot. And thus it does not have a paired strong attack either.

Should the player decide to fill their left-hand slot with a duplicate of the same paired weapon, then like with singular weapons, they will gain access to the paired moveset on the (by default) / / inputs, while also maintaining access to one-handed normal attacks using the / / inputs, and one-handed strong attacks with the / / + inputs.
→ This also allows the player to maintain quick access to multiple different skills and affinities while dual wielding.

→ (Note: that the skill on the weapon in the right-side armament-slot will be prioritized over the left-side, and that dual-wielding in this manner will not give access to the unique paired heavy attacks.)

topics.title: Guard Boost
summary: Guard Boost is a stat in Elden Ring.

It decreases the damage to Stamina received when guarding by an equivalent percentage, i.e. a +0 Dagger with its 15 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.15)=85 Stamina damage when guarding while a +0 Brass Shield with its 61 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.61)=39 Stamina damage when guarding. For 200 base Stamina damage the equivalent numbers would be 200*(1-0.15)=170 Stamina damage for the Dagger and 200*(1-0.61)=78 Stamina damage for the Brass Shield.

topics.title: Critical Attack
summary: Critical Attacks are a variety of special attacks in Elden Ring that cause roughly 2.5 to 4 times as much damage as a regular attack, while also locking both the player and the affected enemy into a long animation.

Certain weapons, including almost all Claws and Daggers, have an increased Critical multiplier, increasing the damage of the Critical Attack by the stat divided by 100 (e.g. for the Miséricorde its large Critical multiplier of 140 is divided by 100 to get 1.4, which means it deals 40% extra damage on Critical Attacks).

The Attack Power of a Critical Attack is dependent on weapon type, and Ripostes usually have about 25-30% more Attack Power than Backstabs. Against small foes such as Vulgar Militia both Backstabs and Ripostes have the same amount of Attack Power and this number is about 15-25% higher than a regular Riposte. Ripostes against large foes such as Omen, Golems, and Bosses have even higher Attack Power, and always (except for Throwing Blades) receive two hits during a Riposte.

topics.title: Skill: Parry
summary: Skill: Parry is a Skill in Elden Ring.

text: Can be granted to infusable Small or Medium Shields, Curved or Thrusting Swords, Daggers and Throwing Blades, Claws, and Fists with the Ash of War: Parry.
Innate skill of many Small Shields and Medium Shields, and one Dagger.
→ Small Shields: Gilded Iron Shield, Perfumer's Shield, Red Thorn Roundshield, Rickety Shield, Rift Shield, Riveted Wooden Shield, Scripture Wooden Shield, and Spiralhorn Shield.

If performed at the right time against an enemy attack that can be parried, it will deflect it, instantly staggering them and potentially opening them up for a Critical Attack. If performed too early or too late, it will instead partially block the attack, which causes the user to suffer intense Stamina drain and to take some damage. As such, depending on the weapon, Parry has different properties, as categorized below:
For Medium Shields, the user holds the shield up and swipes it from right-to-left. This can be referred as Medium Shield Parry.
For Small Shields, the animation is similar to that of Medium Shields. This can be referred as Small Shield Parry.
For Throwing Blades and Thrusting Swords, the user holds the weapon upright and swipes it from right-to-left. This can be referred as Weapon Parry.
For Fists and Claws, the user uses their hand and swats at the air from right-to-left. This can be referred as Hand Parry.
For Curved Swords, the user spins the weapon in flourish. Unlike other parry types, it cannot partially guard enemy attacks immediately upon activation. This can be referred as Curved Sword Parry.
For Daggers, the user holds the weapon up, then twirls the weapon and swiping from right-to-left. This can be referred as Dagger Parry.

topics.title: Guard Counter
summary: The Guard Counter is gameplay mechanic in Elden Ring and ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN.

text: Guard counters allow the player to perform a counter attack after blocking an enemy's attack. To perform a guard counter, the player must block an attack and them immediately press the heavy attack button. If done correctly, a sound effect will play and your character will do a unique attacking animation that is usually faster than the typical heavy attack.
The main purpose of a guard counter is to not only retaliate after blocking an attack, but to deal heavy Stance damage to your opponent and potentially open them up to a ripsote.
Any weapon or tool capable of blocking is capable of doing a guard counter, even if that means having to two-hand it.
Only weapons in the player's right hand can perform a guard counter.

topics.title: Torrent
summary: Torrent is a spectral steed and the player's mount in Elden Ring.

text: Torrent is a spectral steed resembling a horse with two short horns on his head and a white mane. Prior to meeting the Tarnished, he is in the company of Melina. The pair find the Tarnished unconscious in the Stranded Graveyard, where Melina reassures Torrent before granting the Tarnished two flasks. Later, when the Tarnished enters into an accord with Melina, she grants them the Spectral Steed Whistle which allows them to call upon Torrent, revealing that Torrent has chosen them.

Torrent has a taste for Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and Frozen Raisins, which can be used to restore his health. He had a former master who also gave Ranni the Witch the Spirit Calling Bell to pass onto his next master. The identity of this individual is not currently known.

Should the Tarnished choose to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame and incinerate the Erdtree, a final cutscene will show Melina picking up the Spectral Steed Whistle, which disintegrates in her hand (though the player still has access to it in-game).

The player can acquire Torrent from Melina at any time by either resting at the Gatefront Ruins or Agheel Lake North sites of grace or after touching three different sites of grace then resting at any of the additional graces:

Besides allowing a player to get around relatively quickly, Torrent also doesn't appear to take fall damage from certain heights. This allows one to easily jump down from heights that'd normally kill the player as long as they're mounted on Torrent. That said, Torrent isn't immune to dying from jumping from too high of a height: even if a double jump is used to get to a lower level, if the starting point is too high up, Torrent will dissipate on landing and the player will die from the impact.

Jumping again while in mid-air will cause Torrent to perform a second jump. This can only be done once until he touches the ground again and can be used to change direction at the moment of the second jump.

Players can also fight from horseback against enemies, such as shooting arrows or casting spells. However, only one of the player's weapons can be used at a time as the left hand is constantly occupied holding Torrent's reigns, it is still possible to switch between the right-hand and left-hand armament while riding by using the same input the player uses to two-hand their weapons.

Note that it is not possible to change from wielding a weapon one-handed to two-handed while mounted. It is however possible to get the bonuses of two-handing by performing the action before mounting up.
Spirit springs can be used by jumping while riding Torrent to reach higher altitudes. Landing on or close to a spirit spring will completely negate fall damage.

Torrent's HP can be restored by consuming Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and Frozen Raisins. Using a Flask of Crimson Tears will also restore his health on top of the player's own, however only while the player is riding him. If Torrent is killed, using the Spectral Steed Whistle will bring up a prompt to expend a single charge of the Flask of Crimson Tears to revive him.

topics.title: Rebirth
summary: Rebirth (commonly known as respeccing) is a mechanic featured in Elden Ring. Allowing the player to allocate points into different Attributes points during the game.
It is unlocked after defeating Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and is located next to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library Sites of Grace.

text: Rebirthing requires one Larval Tear.

It is important to note that the players starting origin (I.E Samurai, Vagabond, or Astrologer) serves as the starting basis in terms of stat allocation for Rebirthing. Meaning that a player who started as a Samurai will have 12 Vigor points invested already while an Astrologer will start with 6 Vigor points. All points earned up to the level the player is currently at must be allocated for rebirth.
If the player chooses to cancel their Rebirthing, they will not lose a Larval Tear.

topics.title: Mechanics
summary: Within the lands of Elden Ring are scattered various important elements the player should make themselves aware of.

text: Runes can be obtained by defeating enemies or using items. Runes are used to level up your character's Stats and Attributes, buy items, and strengthen weapons and armor.
There are rest points called Sites of Grace.

Resting at a Site of Grace will restore your HP, FP, and heal any status ailments. It will also refill all of your Sacred Flasks. Most of the enemies you have defeated will be revived when you rest at a Site of Grace.
[How to use a Site of Grace]
Approach the Site of Grace and press the [△/Y] button to activate it.
From here, pressing the [△/Y] button will bring up the menu and let you rest.
Sites of Grace that you have not reached yet emit rays of light.
[Site of Grace menu]
The Site of Grace menu is available while resting.
The selections available will change as the story progresses.
{| class="wikitable"
|Pass Time||Move time forward in the game.
|Level Up||Enhance your character’s stats.
|Add Charge to Flask||Increase the number of times you can use the flask.
|Increase Amount Replenished by Flasks||Enhance the flask’s restorative effect.
|Distribute Flask Charges||Allocate the number of charges for your sacred flasks.
| Memorize Spell||Equip magic you have learned in the memory slots to use it in the game. The number of slots available depends on your character’s status.
|Mix Wondrous Physick||Mix acquired Crystal Tears to customize the effects of Flask of Wondrous Physick.
|Sort Chest||Store items in or remove items from the chest.

Sites of Grace that you already discovered will be saved on the map. Select the Site of Grace you want to travel to on the map, and you will move to that location. You cannot travel while in some dungeons.
[Guidance of Grace]
The light emanating from some Sites of Grace gives a hint as to where you may want to go next.
The Guidance of Grace can also be found in the map menu.
When a rebirth monument is nearby and a monument icon is shown on the left side of the screen, you can use ashes to summon a spirit.
The summoned spirit will leave when its HP reaches zero, when a boss is defeated, when the spirit moves a certain distance away from the monument, or when the same ashes are used again.
Only one type of spirit can be summoned at a time, and spirits cannot be summoned during multiplayer.
Upon dying, you will be revived at the last Site of Grace at which you rested. However, if you died near a Stake of Marika, you can choose to be revived there instead.
You can confirm if you are in the area of effect of a Stake of Marika by checking if the status icon (bow and arrow icon) appears.
Use the Spectral Steed Whistle to summon a Spectral Steed to ride.
If the Spectral Steed dies it can be summoned again, but it will consume a Flask of Crimson Tears.
You can see your current location, terrain, buildings, and other information. Markers and landmarks can be placed on the map.
You can also go to a Site of Grace that you have discovered from the map menu.
You cannot open the map when you are engaged in battle.
Use the Birdseye Telescopes in each area to see into the distance like a bird and get a better view of your destination.
A character dies when their HP reaches zero.
When you die, all the runes you are carrying will be dropped. You can retrieve them by going back to the location of your death. If you die again before retrieving them, they will be lost.

topics.title: Runes
summary: Runes () act as both the currency and experience points (XP) in Elden Ring.

One of the main game mechanics behind runes is that they'll be lost on death and the only way to get them back is to return to the area where they were lost to reclaim them. However, if one should die before they can retrieve the lost runes, they'll be lost permanently.

Runes are gained when killing enemies, but also exist as objects which can be picked up and are sometimes dropped by defeated enemies. These rune objects exist in various forms, which provide increasing numbers of runes when used or sold to merchants (for the same number of runes as when used). The various forms of these rune objects, in increasing order of how many runes they provide, are: Golden Rune 1, Golden Rune 2, Golden Rune 3, Golden Rune 4, Golden Rune 5, Golden Rune 6, Golden Rune 7, Golden Rune 8, Lands Between Rune, Golden Rune 9, Golden Rune 10, Golden Rune 11, Golden Rune 12, Golden Rune 13, Numen's Rune, Hero's Rune 1, Hero's Rune 2, Hero's Rune 3, Hero's Rune 4, Hero's Rune 5, Lord's Rune

text: Unlike dungeon boss fights, if one dies inside an evergaol, the runes will be retrievable on the surface/entrance area to the evergaol so there's minimal risk in fighting bosses in evergaols.
Golden Runes and any other item that grants runes are not lost on death so it's best to keep them in their object state until ready to level up or buy something to minimize rune losses
Sacrificial Twigs can be used in a talisman slot so on the next death, the twig is lost rather than one's runes.

topics.title: Great Runes
summary: Great Runes (大ルーン, Dai Rūn) are the shards of the Elden Ring which were inherited by some of the demigods. The great strength they granted tainted the demigods, compelling them to war over control of the Lands Between.
The Tarnished can retrieve Great Runes by slaying their respective Shardbearers, which can then be activated at their corresponding Divine Tower.

text: The Great Runes are the shards of the Elden Ring, currently making up the Golden Order, and represent the concepts of order and discipline that the demigods enforced on the physical world. They were inherited by some of the demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal following the shattering of the Elden Ring. The mad taint of the newfound strength granted by the Great Runes precipitated the Shattering, wherein the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. The demigods who inherited Great Runes were known as Shardbearers.

Most great Runes can be equipped in their slot at a Site of Grace, appearing next to the status bars. Once equipped, a Rune Arc must be consumed to activate its effects, indicated by the rune lighting up. The effect lasts until death.
Changing the equipped Great Rune will also deactivate it.
While summoned in another world, Great Runes have no effect and dying while summoned does not deactivate the Great Rune's effect back in your world.
As they are key items, Great Runes will be lost upon entering New Game Plus and, once re-obtained, have to be restored again.
Ranni's Great Rune (mentioned only)
It is unknown if the Rune of Death is considered a Great Rune.

The Great Runes reflect the demigods that inherited them. For example, Morgott's Great Rune was proof that he was born of the Golden Lineage, and the rightful Lord of Leyndell. Mohg, Lord of Blood's Great Rune was soaked with accursed blood from his devout love for the wretched mire he was born into. Morgott's and Mohg's Great Runes were naturally similar due to their bearers being twins. Malenia, Blade of Miquella's Great Rune was half-rotted but infused with Malenia's spirit of resistance.

Miquella of the Haligtree and Ranni the Witch are the only Shardbearers known to have discarded their Great Runes. The whereabouts of Ranni's Great Rune remain unknown. Miquella relinquishes and breaks his Great Rune after the Tarnished crosses into one of three areas of the Land of Shadow: the eastern half of Scadu Altus, the Rauh Base region, or Shadow Keep.

The Tarnished, upon returning to the Lands Between, were compelled by the Two Fingers to seek out demigods to relieve them of their Great Runes in order to become Elden Lord. The Tarnished required one Great Rune to be granted audience with the Two Fingers in the inner chamber of the Roundtable Hold. They also required enough Great Runes to repair the Elden Ring before the Two Fingers would permit them to enter Leyndell, Royal Capital to have an audience with Queen Marika to become Elden Lord. During the course of the game, this is two Great Runes, however since the Shardbearer Morgott, the Omen King guards the entrance to the Erdtree and must be killed to access it, they will have at least three when granted audience. Finger Reader Enia has only ever seen two Great Runes together once before this.

When initially obtained by the player, a Great Rune (except the Great Rune of the Unborn) would be devoid of any benediction, and had to be taken to the Divine Tower mentioned in its description, whereupon it would be restored by interacting with the image of the Great Rune above the inert Two Fingers at the summit of the tower. Further, a Rune Arc was required for The Tarnished (Protagonist) to be granted the blessing of a Great Rune after restoring it.
The Great Runes acquired by The Tarnished were used to repair the Elden Ring in at least one ending.

summary: Flask of Crimson Tears is a refillable tool in Elden Ring.

text: Quest Reward: Stranded Graveyard (Limgrave)
Automatically acquired after reaching the Stranded Graveyard at the start of the game.
Restores between 250 (at +0) and 810 (at +12) HP when used, expending 1 charge. This also heals Torrent for the same amount.

→ The player starts with 4 charges and a maximum of 14 total charges can be held between this flask and the Flask of Cerulean Tears.

→→ A total amount of 30 Golden Seeds are needed to gain 14 charges. Roughly 47 Golden Seeds can be found throughout the game in a single Journey, well in excess of this amount.

The potency of the flask can be permanently increased by +1 (up to +12) by expending Sacred Tears at a Site of Grace.
→ Restores 250 HP at +0, 345 HP at +1, 430 HP at +2, 505 HP at +3, 570 HP at +4, 625 HP at +5, 670 HP at +6, 700 HP at +7, 730 HP at +8, 755 HP at +9, 780 HP at +10, 795 HP at +11, and 810 HP at +12.

summary: New Game Plus, alternatively known as New Game+, NG+, Playthrough, or Journey, is the system used by Elden Ring to determine how many times a character has defeated the final boss and started the game again with their old equipment at a higher difficulty.

text: Upon defeating the final boss you will get the option to "Begin Journey 2" when sitting at the Table of Lost Grace Site of Grace in Roundtable Hold. Selecting this option will prompt you to answer Yes or No as to whether or not you'd like to advance to New Game+.

topics.title: Online
summary: Online is a gameplay mode in Elden Ring. Bringing in aspects of cooperative, casual competitive play along with Invasions.

Multiplayer mainly takes on two distinct forms, there is the standard variant, which is spontaneous and extremely variable in intensity and complexity and then there is the more fore-planned Arena Matches.

text: [Cross-Region Play]
Perform Matchmaking: Makes it possible to play with other players from across the world with no region-based restrictions.

No Matchmaking: Disables the user's ability to play with other players outside of the their own designated region. The size of these regions vary greatly, as some may contain several countries at once like America, Europe or Africa, yet the singular country of Japan gets their very own region. This feature is greatly reduced on PC as it effectively only has two regions it can group players into; Japan and everywhere else.
[Send Summon Signs]
Enable: Prevents one's own summon signs from appearing in worlds with an Adversary present.
Disable: Allows one's own summon signs to appear in worlds with Adversaries present.
[Voice Chat]
This option is absent on the PC version of Elden Ring.
Allowed: Enables in-game voice chat.
Restricted: Disables in-game voice chat.
[Display Player Names]
Controls what name will appear above the health bars of other players. This option absent on the PC version of Elden Ring.
Character name: Displays the name that player chose for their character on the in-game Character Creation screen.
Online ID: Displays the player's PSN or XBOX username/gamertag.
[Launch Settings]
This setting controls whether the game automatically attempts to log-on to the official Elden Ring Online servers after crossing the "PRESS ANY BUTTON" prompt on the title screen.
Play Online:
Play Offline:

This option is automatically set to "Play Online" at the start of a new profile, meaning players who have a functioning connection but are adamant to play specifically in Offline mode need to manually set it to "Play Offline" then either make a character first then quit to return to the title screen or turn the game off then boot it back up again. Starting the game in Offline mode adds a "LOG IN" prompt amongst the "CONTINUE", "LOAD GAME" and "NEW GAME" options on the main menu.
[Data User Agreement]
Details your consent to the game's Data User Agreement.
Accept:
Decline:
Located in it's own designated Multiplayer menu. Passwords are used to isolate potential connections and make it easier for specific players to connect with each other.
[Multiplayer Password]

Hosts who have inserted a multiplayer password may only be able to see the Summon Signs of players who have the same password and likewise the Summon Signs of a Guest with a password can only be seen by Hosts carrying the same password.

This option also completely removes Player-Level and Weapon-Upgrade-based matchmaking, allowing vastly under-leveled or over-leveled guests to join a host's world. Over-leveled guests will have their stats reduced in an attempt of preserving game-balance, though the effectiveness of this down-scaling varies greatly based on the Host's level compared to the guest and what kind of build the guest is using. Under-leveled guests do not get their stats scaled upwards.
[Group Password]

Players can have a total of five active group passwords at a time. They do not influence the matchmaking system in any way and only serve as a means of letting players know that a Player Phantom, Message, Bloodstain or Summon Sign came from someone carrying the same Group Password. Players accomplishing a significant feat of progression in their own game will also let everyone carrying the same group passwords as them know of this feat while at the same time distributing a rune-boosting buff to those same players.
Online has a number of passive features that are present at all times and require no direct input from the player to appear. These features include:
[Player Phantoms]
Spectral afterimages of other players exploring and interacting with the world in their own game. The moments captured are mere recent short recordings of their journey and are not quite real-time.

Outside of being a reminder than in some way one is never truly alone in the adventure, these momentary glimpses into the lives of other players may directly assist the person witnessing them in revealing potential secrets such as a seeing a phantom appear just as it walks through an Illusory Wall that the witness wasn't initially aware of themselves.
[Messages]
Players may leave messages comprised of differing combinations of preset words and phrases to either assist, deceive or lighten the mood of any other player who may come across them and read them.

Should a message leave a strong enough impression for the reader to rate them Good or Poor, either option results in the writer (should they be playing at the moment of rating) receiving a decent chunk of their HP healed.
[Bloodstains]
Bloodstains appear at the location of a player's death. They are five second recordings of their last moments before being forcibly sent back to a Sites of Grace.
[Shared Accomplishments]

Should someone with a group password either defeat a Shardbearer or reach the Credits screen in their playthrough, every other player who shares the same group password as them will receive a buff that increases the amount of Runes received from fallen enemies by 5% for five minutes.

tables.Allies: Host of Fingers; The Host of Fingers serves as the anchor-point of the session, they are the ones who decide when to begin and the session cannot continue once the host is either dead or has disconnected from the servers. Their primary goal is to to defeat a boss, once the boss is defeated the session will automatically end.
tables.Adversaries: Duelist; The Duelist is willingly summoned by the host, their goal is to defeat the host in combat.

tables.Allies: Furled Finger; The Furled Finger acts as an ally for the host, their primary goal is to help the Host defeat a boss.
tables.Adversaries: Invader; The Invader has the ability to forcibly join the Host's session once the host has either successfully summoned a cooperator or used the Taunter's Tongue, the Invader's goal is to defeat the host before the host either defeats an overworld boss or traverses a dungeon boss's mist.

tables.Allies: Hunter; When an invader has arrived in the world of the Host of Fingers, through the use of the White Cipher Ring the host can automatically summon a Hunter to assist in the battle against the adversary. The Hunter's mission will be complete when the invader has been vanquished.
tables.Adversaries: Invader; The Invader has the ability to forcibly join the Host's session once the host has either successfully summoned a cooperator or used the Taunter's Tongue, the Invader's goal is to defeat the host before the host either defeats an overworld boss or traverses a dungeon boss's mist.

text: For the sake of balance the game will primarily search for guests that are within a certain radius of the Host's character level as well as and the highest upgraded weapon the players has ever obtained. It does not matter if said weapon has been stored or even discarded, even if the player has completely removed access to said upgraded weapon the game will still count that weapon's level to their matchmaking radius.
[Character Level]
[Weapon Upgrade Level]
[Flask Count]
For the sake of balancing, multiplayer alters how many flasks charges different players have and how these charges are replenished based on what role said player is currently in.

The Hosts of Fingers will keep their maximum flask count and guests will have their flasks charges cut by half of what it usually is in their own world. If a guest's flask-count is an odd number in their own world then it will be rounded down to an even number when visiting another host's world, so if a guest wants to maximize their flask-count they should try to allot both of their flasks into an even number whenever possible.
[Replenishing Flasks]
Allies can have their flasks replenished from vanquishing enemy groups, killing Crimson Tear Scarabs and defeating Invaders.

Meanwhile Adversaries will have their flasks replenished from the death of any other player, whether it be a Furled Finger, Hunter or even a fellow Invader. The death of the Host of Fingers does not replenish flasks however as it will end the session anyway.
